data.content_ref: inline:The claimed reduction does not obviously follow, and the refutation conditions reveal the failure: SRC_001's registry-size account would be refuted exactly when guarded modules had many mutations AND the asymmetry persisted—but SRC_004's order-effect account would still explain that persistence as a sequence artifact (wrong installation order preventing manifestation of the selective effect despite high mutation density). Thus the size account and the order account are orthogonal rather than reductive: size determines whether a selective effect is measurable, order determines whether the mutation stream allows it to manifest. The target presupposes that size acts as the determinant of order's efficacy, but a high-mutation module can still exhibit order-dependent outcomes, proving the order effect operates independently of size and is not merely a special case of the size constraint.
